what: What a FRESH Titanium Bot install seeds into the proxy's database (PROVIDERS-1). Read once by `node cp/cli.mjs proxy seed`. An install that already has rows is never re-seeded, and after the seed this file is history: providers, keys and plan models are managed from the Providers panel at api.titanium.bot/admin.
holdsNoValue: Every credential here is named by its os.environ NAME only. There is no key value in this file, there must never be one, and tests/proxy-deploy.test.mjs fails the build if anything in it looks like a credential. The environment names are the fresh-install bootstrap only; a live key is added, rolled and removed through the panel.
order: Seed in this order and nothing else works: credentials, then plan models (deployments), then the fallback map. MEASURED on this Mac 2026-09-08 against litellm-database:v1.100.0, POST /fallback answers 400 'Invalid fallback models' when the fallback target is not a model_name the proxy currently serves, so the vision deployment has to exist before its pair can be registered.

catalog.note: The vendor's own /models is the only live list. MEASURED on grok-bot-local-vm 2026-09-08 it answers 10 ids carrying id, object, created and owned_by and NOTHING else: no context window, no vision flag, no label. A Refresh gives the operator names and only names, and the panel says so in those words. It is read through a LiteLLM pass-through carrying the vendor key as a header, so the control plane gets a live catalog while holding no vendor key. Register the pass-through with include_subpath true or the subpath answers 404 (measured).
No /models endpoint is reached through the LiteLLM minimax provider, so the picker is the curated list below and the panel says the list is curated rather than live.

seed false: the provider row is written, no credential and no plan model are. Jason has rotated the Alibaba key and is putting the new one in Bitwarden as QWEN_API_KEY. The moment it is synced to ~/.api_keys the panel's add-key action takes it; nothing here has to change.

planModels.note: model_name is the ALIAS and is a contract with every box already pointed at it: created once, never renamed. vendorModel is the thing that changes when Z.AI retires a model, and POST /model/update merges, so a repoint preserves the credential, the costs and every tb_ key (measured).

A ROUTING TARGET, never a card. customerVisible false and no customer label, and the control plane DROPS a plan model like this from the customer's Settings list rather than falling back to the id. That single rule is what stops a 'plan-zai-vision (included with your plan)' card appearing the next time a workspace is minted.

visionFallback points at itself only because this model takes an image itself; the panel requires a vision fallback on every plan model and a model that needs none names itself. POST /fallback refuses a self-pair (400 'cannot be its own fallback'), so the seed writes no fallback row for this one.

fallbacks.note: A request the flagship refuses because it carries an image (Z.AI code 1210) is retried once here before the customer sees anything. The customer's key names plan-zai; the fallback is the router's own move and is not a second model the key has to be allowed.

defaults.note: The plan model a NEW workspace is given. The super admin changes it in the Providers panel and it is stored in the control plane's admin_settings, not here: this value is only what a fresh install starts from.

tenantKeyRoutes.note: The per-key door list every tenant key is minted with, and the backfill applies to every key already in the field. It is what replaced general_settings.allowed_routes and what closes PROXY-8. MEASURED on this Mac 2026-09-08: a key carrying this list answers 403 on /key/info, /model/info, /model_group/info and /health while chat completions and /v1/models still answer 200. Add a path here only with the same care: a box that needs a route it does not have gets a 403 with no other clue.

reservedPassThroughs.note: PROXY-3, the second TinyFish subscription. A pass-through cannot pool two keys the way a model_name pools two deployments, so a second subscription is a second PAIR of paths and the control plane decides which pair a tenant is given at mint. The names are decided here so nobody invents a third; the pair is not registered until TINYFISH_API_KEY_2 exists, because a pass-through whose os.environ name is unset forwards the literal string 'os.environ/NAME' to the vendor as the key (measured).
